I have been a Citi cardholder since XXXX. My original credit limit was {$16000.00}. Since then, Citi has repeatedly reduced my available credit despite my continued efforts to maintain my account. 

My credit limit has been reduced as follows : * Original credit limit : {$16000.00} * XX/XX/XXXX : Reduced to {$12000.00} * XX/XX/XXXX : Reduced to {$12000.00} * XX/XX/XXXX : Reduced to {$11000.00} Each time Citi reduced my credit limit, my required minimum monthly payment increased significantly. The repeated credit limit reductions have also substantially increased my credit utilization ratio, causing my credit score to decline through no fault of my own. As a result, I have been unable to qualify for credit with other lenders or have been denied credit because my credit score no longer accurately reflects my payment history and overall creditworthiness. 

Citi has stated that the reductions were based on XXXX or more of my accounts being past due and because payments were low on XXXX or more of my accounts. I do not believe this explanation justifies the repeated reductions. 

I have never been more than XXXX days late with Citi or any other creditor. If I do not make my payment by Citis due date, I am already assessed a late fee of approximately {$41.00}. That is the contractual penalty for a late payment. Reducing my credit limit afterward effectively penalizes me a second time by increasing my credit utilization, lowering my credit score, increasing my minimum monthly payment, and limiting my ability to obtain credit elsewhere.

Therefore, I do not understand how Citi can cite low payments as a basis for repeatedly reducing my credit limit when I have met the minimum payment requirements established under my cardholder agreement. 

These repeated credit limit reductions have created a harmful cycle. By lowering my available credit while I carry a balance, Citi has artificially increased my utilization ratio, damaged my credit profile, increased my required monthly payment, reduced my ability to qualify for additional credit, and made it more difficult for me to improve my financial situation. Rather than encouraging responsible repayment, these actions have made repayment more burdensome.

I am a Bank of America credit card customer of several decades, currently holding three accounts in good standing with a consistent history of on-time payments and large balance transfers. This complaint concerns Bank of America 's failure to adequately notify me that a payment was past due on one of my accounts, and the bank 's subsequent refusal to remediate the credit reporting harm that resulted.

Each month I received Bank of America 's standard electronic statement notification email. The subject line read " you have a new statement. '' The body of the email displayed the account balance and minimum payment due. At no point did the subject line or body of these emails indicate that the account was past due, that a payment had been missed, or that the account was at risk of being reported delinquent to the credit bureaus. A reasonable customer reviewing these notifications would not be alerted to a delinquency.

Earlier this year I attempted to set up autopay on the account, which carried a balance of {$290.00}, to prevent exactly this kind of oversight. I was unable to locate the autopay setup feature on the Bank of America website despite reasonable effort. When I later called Bank of America to discuss this matter, the representative confirmed that the autopay setup feature is difficult to locate on the website. I still have not been able to locate it independently. 

I was not notified of the delinquency by Bank of America in any form that I noticed. I learned of the issue only when the credit reporting agencies notified me that my credit score had dropped by a range of XXXX to XXXX points due to a 30-day late notation on the XX/XX/year> payment for this account. 

I contacted Bank of America by phone. The representative confirmed the facts above, set up autopay for the full balance during the call, and the account is being brought current. I asked whether Bank of America would request that the credit bureaus remove the 30-day late notation in light of the circumstances and my customer history. I was told this was not possible.

I am requesting that Bank of America ( a ) contact the credit bureaus currently reporting this notation and request removal of the 30-day late mark as a goodwill adjustment, in light of my decades-long customer relationship and the notification and user-interface failures described above, ( b ) review the design of its electronic statement notification emails to ensure that past-due status is clearly disclosed in the subject line and body of the email, so that other customers are not similarly affected, and ( c ) fix its website which is difficult to navigate for purposes of making payments and setting up autopay.

An FTC Identity Theft Report is not a casual statement. The FTC explains that the Identity Theft Report is generated through XXXX, is submitted under penalty of perjury, is made available to law enforcement, and is designed to notify businesses that their records XXXX contain fraudulent information about the consumer. The FCRA definition of an identity theft report includes an official valid report filed with an appropriate federal, state, or local law enforcement agency or other government agency deemed appropriate, where false filing can carry criminal penalties.

Those are exactly the types of identifying information that can be misused in identity theft. 

My complaint concerns identity theft and consumer liability. Midlands response does not show a reasonable investigation into identity theft. 

XXXX is also a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies. Under FCRA 623, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 6 ), furnishers must have reasonable procedures to respond to identity-theft block notices from credit reporting agencies and prevent refurnishing blocked identity-theft information. The credit reporting agencies were also required under FCRA 605B, 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ( b ), to notify XXXX that the information may be the result of identity theft, that an identity theft report was filed, that a block was requested, and the effective dates of the block. I do not know if it is fees, interest, or something else. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), specifically 15 U.S.C. Section 1692f ( 1 ), a debt collector is not allowed to collect any amount on top of the original debt unless it is authorized by the original agreement or allowed by law. I never got anything from Sunrise breaking this down, so I do not believe this higher balance is accurate or legal. 

Problem 2 I never received a debt validation notice The law ( FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. Section 1692g ) says that when a debt collector first contacts you, they have to send you a written notice within 5 days that tells you the amount of the debt, who the original creditor is, and that you have 30 days to dispute it. I never received anything like that from Sunrise Credit Service at any point. If they can not show they sent me this notice, that is a violation of the law, and I do not believe they have the right to be reporting this on my credit.

Problem 3 I do not know if Sunrise even legally owns this debt For a collection company to put something on my credit report, they need to have actually been assigned the debt from the original creditor. I never got any notice that XXXX XXXX sold or transferred my account to Sunrise Credit Service. I have no way to confirm this debt was properly transferred, and Sunrise has never provided me with any documentation proving they have the legal right to collect it. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. Section 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), a company can not report information to a credit bureau if it has reason to believe that information is inaccurate. Without proof of a valid assignment, I do not think this account should be on my report.

Problem 4 The payment history on my report is incomplete Looking at my XXXX  report, this collection only shows payment activity for XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, with everything else listed as 'Data Unavailable. ' That is not a complete or accurate history, and the FCRA ( Section 1681s-2 ( b ) ) requires that information reported to credit bureaus be accurate and complete. My dispute specifically invoked the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) ) and Texas Finance Code 392.202. I formally disputed the alleged debt in its entirety and demanded that CMS cease all collection activity until proper validation was provided.

In my written dispute, I specifically requested the following documentation and disclosures : 1. The name and physical mailing address of the original creditor.

To whom it XXXX concern, I am writing to dispute the Claim ID XXXX for {$53.00} opened on XX/XX/year>. The merchandise received is different from the merchant 's description and is defective/unfit for its intended purpose. 

Summary of Misrepresentation : The merchants website advertises this " XXXX XXXX '' using images that depict a roll of flexible tape. Based on these professional images, a consumer reasonably expects a product with the properties of tapespecifically flexibility and adhesion. However, the product received is functionally useless : The product page for the " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX '' presents a fundamental conflict between its marketing title and technical specifications. While the title prominently uses the word " Metallic, '' which implies a high-sheen, reflective, and brilliant finish, the body text contradicts this by describing a " soft satin finish. '' In the context of professional cake decorating, these terms represent two entirely different aesthetic tiers. A bank claim can be supported by the argument of Material Misrepresentation, as the merchant used a high-value descriptive keyword to trigger a sale while delivering a product that lacks the primary light-reflective properties promised in the heading. 

Furthermore, there is a significant discrepancy regarding the product 's structural performance. The primary marketing photograph depicts the ribbon as a rigid or semi-rigid material capable of holding sharp, upright loops and architectural folds on a cake. Conversely, the description labels the material as " soft and flexible '' edible lace. Physics dictates that a soft, lace-like material can not maintain the structural integrity shown in the photo without internal support, which is not mentioned. This constitutes Deceptive Visual Advertising, as the consumer is induced to purchase based on a " structural '' use case that the actual physical material is incapable of performing.

The listing further fails the consumer by utilizing subjective terminology in place of technical dimensions. By labeling the ribbon as " Wide '' without providing specific measurements in inches or millimeters, the merchant creates a " dimensional ambiguity '' that makes it impossible for a professional to determine if the item is fit for their specific project. In banking disputes, this is categorized as a Failure of Disclosure. Without exact specifications, the term " Wide '' is a subjective claim rather than a factual description, leading to a purchase of an item that may not meet the necessary physical requirements for the intended application.

Transparency regarding safety is also a major fault, as the page lacks a visible ingredient list or allergy warning. For an edible product, particularly one using black and metallic pigments, which often contain iron oxides or specific dyes ( like Red 40 ), the omission of this data is a critical safety gap. The bank 's argument for Non-Disclosure of Essential Safety Information is highly effective here ; a consumer can not be expected to accept an " edible '' product if they can not verify its contents against dietary restrictions or legal food safety standards prior to the transaction.

Finally, the merchant employs a restrictive " No Returns '' policy for food items, which conflicts with their categorization of the item as " Equipment and Supplies. '' This creates a " Liability Shield '' where the merchant avoids accountability for the products failure to perform, like the equipment shown in the photos. A bank claim can argue that this is an Unfair Trade Practice, as the merchant is using the " food '' classification to bypass consumer protection rights when the product fails to meet the " professional grade '' quality standards they advertised. By proving the product is materially different from its description, the merchants " No Return '' policy becomes legally unenforceable in a dispute.

1. Misleading " Metallic '' Representation The primary selling point is the " Metallic '' finish, but the merchant includes a contradictory fine-print disclaimer.

The Critique : The product name explicitly uses the word " Metallic, '' yet the description admits it is " not as metallic '' as their other products and compares it to a " soft satin ''. This is a bait-and-switch tactic where the title promises a high-shine finish that the merchant knows the product can not achieve.

My argument : " The merchant 's own documentation admits the product does not meet the standard defined by its own title. This is deceptive advertising. '' 2. Unfair " No Returns '' Policy for Defective Goods Evil Cake Genius typically refuses returns on edible items regardless of quality.

The Critique : Consumer protection laws generally state that a " No Returns '' policy can not apply to items that are defective or misrepresented.

On or about XXXX XXXX XXXX, Citibank closed all of my accounts : two checking accounts and a XXXX XXXX account at the bank, along with my associated Citi XXXX XXXX XXXX rollover IRA. Citibank cited an incomplete " Know Your Customer '' ( KYC ) review ( Citi KYC Reference ID XXXX ). The closure cut off my access to my funds and ended a 29-year banking relationship. I am pursuing the brokerage rollover IRA, and the risk that its forced closure triggers tax and early-withdrawal consequences, separately with the appropriate securities regulator ; I note it here only to show the full scope of the closure.

The closure was not the result of any failure to cooperate on my part. The KYC review opened around XX/XX/XXXX. Because my assigned financial advisor ( XXXX XXXX ) failed to advance the process, I personally called Citi 's KYC department on at least three occasions ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX ) and provided every item requested. Citi recorded each of these calls. On these calls I : - Corrected inaccurate information in Citi 's own KYC profile, including a long-dissolved former employer ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX which ceased operations in XXXX ) and a phantom company ( " XXXX XXXX '' ) that Citi had listed as my source of wealth. The correct entity is XXXX XXXX XXXX, my own registered LLC.

- Provided detailed source-of-wealth information and, at Citi 's request, supplied statements from external retirement and brokerage accounts to substantiate that my Citi holdings were consistent with my stated net worth.

- Was told by Citi 's KYC representatives that the review was essentially complete and that no further action was required from me. 

Despite this, Citi issued a closure-warning letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ( closure date XX/XX/XXXX ) and ultimately closed all of my accounts. On XX/XX/XXXX, my Citi Wealth Relationship XXXX emailed me acknowledging that I had been " incredibly cooperative and transparent, '' stating that the closure was unexpected, and confirming that she had escalated the matter to KYC management to seek reopening. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, two members of Citi 's Florida wealth-management leadership called me directly and acknowledged, on a recorded Citi line , that the closure of my accounts was caused by a defect in Citi 's own systems and not by any failure on my part. They confirmed I had cooperated and provided the requested information " each and every time, '' and stated that my accounts were closed even though I had done so. They described this as a recurring " glitch '' in Citi 's systems that they are actively working to repair, stated that it is affecting " far too many '' Citi customers across multiple business lines including Citi Private Bank, and said they had escalated the problem that day to senior Citi operations leadership. They called the treatment of a 29-year relationship " inexcusable, '' and offered to attempt to re-establish my accounts and reverse the resulting charges. XXXX XXXX also committed to send me a written follow-up. This was a management-level admission that my accounts were wrongfully closed by a known, systemic process failure, not for any legitimate compliance reason.

Citi has only partly honored those commitments, and its internal handling remains contradictory. As of the date of this complaint, Citibank has reopened my primary 29-year joint checking account ( ending XXXX ), which I can again use. That reopening, however, was incomplete and left the account functionally impaired by the same systems Citi 's management has admitted are defective : my ATM/debit cards were never reinstated and remained blocked even after the accounts were reopened a defect Citibank discovered only when I happened to flag it on XX/XX/XXXX and my household was silently dropped from the account 's subscription-rebate ( perks ) benefit program when Citi 's system closed and reopened the accounts. Both had to be corrected manually after the fact. The second checking account ( ending XXXX ) remains closed ; it existed only to link my departing IRA, so I do not seek its restoration. The XXXX XXXX account ( ending XXXX ) is open but unfunded. XXXX XXXX never sent the written follow-up or the direct contact information he committed to provide on XX/XX/XXXX, now more than a week ago. On XX/XX/XXXX, two Citi units gave me directly contradictory information on the same day. My wealth relationship manager 's office emailed asking me to re-document my " source of wealth '' on a business questionnaire, while Citi 's KYC department confirmed to me on a recorded call that my source of wealth had already been accepted in XXXX and that the review was " satisfied/approved '' on XX/XX/XXXX with " nothing else needed. '' Closure-related charges have continued, and the disruption from the wrongful closure of a XXXX relationship remains ongoing and unremedied. 

That same evening ( XX/XX/XXXX ), Citibank restricted every one of my accounts again under a new case reference ( XXXX ), hours after its own KYC department had confirmed on a recorded line that the prior review was satisfied and there was no block. The restriction bars deposits, transfers, and withdrawals from my bank accounts and warns that if I do not act, Citibank will liquidate my retirement account and mail me a check. The restriction notice states that my accounts were restricted because I " have not yet provided critical, missing information, '' frames the restriction as something I can " easily lift '' by providing that information, and presents closure as avoidable by a XX/XX/XXXX deadline. It presents the restriction, in other words, as a conditional and preventable consequence within my control. That stated basis is false on Citi 's own record. Citi 's KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day that I had already provided the information, that it was accepted in XXXX, and that there was " no block. '' And on XX/XX/XXXX, my own Citi relationship manager confirmed to me in writing that the restriction is procedural, that the case is simply being finalized internally, and that there is " no new needed information '' from me. Citibank nonetheless imposed the full restriction immediately, on a stated basis its own employees had already disproved. The adverse action was taken first. It was not a future consequence I could avert by supplying anything, because Citi confirms there is nothing left for me to supply. 

Citibank subsequently lifted the restriction on my deposit accounts my joint checking was usable again within days yet it has continued to generate and mail me the same restriction notices. A mailed copy of the XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice reached me about a week later, on or about XX/XX/XXXX. When I called Citibank about it, a representative told me that no further information was needed, that the case was simply being finalized, and that Citibank 's system " will periodically continue to send notices until the case is closed, '' so I should " disregard '' the notice. Citibank is thus mailing a 29-year customer formal notices that state he failed to provide " critical, missing information '' and threaten to liquidate his retirement account, while simultaneously instructing him to ignore those notices because nothing is in fact outstanding. A consumer can not reliably tell a genuine restriction notice from XXXX Citibank will later say to disregard. 

This was still unresolved as of XX/XX/XXXX. Roughly two weeks after Citibank 's representatives first told me the review was in its " final stages, '' I called Citibank 's KYC department again to confirm my status. A representative told me my accounts were unblocked, but that the review remained open and was in a " disposition '' stage that had been handed to another Citibank department for a final approval she could neither see nor expedite, with no further information needed from me. She again offered to request a written " KYC satisfied '' letter once the review closes a letter I have asked for repeatedly and still do not have. To date, Citibank has never rescinded its XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice in writing. That notice still states on its face that my Citi accounts will be closed, and my retirement account liquidated and mailed to me as a check, if I do not provide information by XX/XX/XXXX the very notice Citibank 's representatives have told me to disregard because nothing is in fact outstanding. More than two weeks after Citibank 's personnel began telling me the matter was in its " final stages, '' Citibank still has not given me a single authoritative written answer reconciling that standing closure-and-liquidation notice with its assurances that I owe it nothing further.

Underlying every step of this is a single, systemic failure : Citibank 's automated KYC and account-closure processes took adverse action against a fully compliant 29-year customer, repeated it, and would not release it and no person at Citibank has been able to stop or override it. My assigned financial advisor wrote to me that the closure was " beyond our control. '' My relationship manager advocated for me for weeks, including on weekends and after hours, yet the restriction persisted and the false notices kept arriving. Citibank 's own Florida wealth-management leadership admitted the closure was a system defect, said they had escalated it to senior bank-operations leadership, and still could neither prevent the renewed restriction nor stop Citibank 's systems from mailing me notices they themselves told me to disregard to the point that, in XXXX XXXX, a senior Citibank manager was reduced to escalating internally to try to switch off the bank 's automated " missing information '' messages, which the system continued to generate by default. When a bank 's own advisor, relationship manager, and senior management all acknowledge the customer did nothing wrong and still can not stop the bank 's systems from closing his accounts, freezing his retirement assets, and mailing him false liquidation threats, the failure is systemic not the error of any one employee.

I am asking the CFPB to require Citibank to : ( 1 ) produce the recordings of my XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX KYC calls under Reference ID XXXX, and the XX/XX/XXXX call from its wealth-management leadership ; ( 2 ) explain the basis for closing and then restricting my accounts after its own representatives confirmed my compliance and after its own management attributed the closure to a system defect, including how it could restrict my accounts for " missing information '' that its own KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day, and that its own relationship manager confirmed in writing on XX/XX/XXXX, had already been provided and accepted ; ( 3 ) reverse any fees or third-party charges ( e.g., stop-payment fees ) caused by the closure ; ( 4 ) correct the inaccurate source-of-wealth/employment records that drove the adverse action ; and ( 5 ) given Citi management 's own statement that this defect is affecting " far too many '' customers, examine whether other consumers have been subjected to the same wrongful closures.

I deposited two business checks at a Wells Fargo branch and was informed that the funds would be subject to a seven-business-day hold. Due to a federal holiday and intervening weekends, this results in a delay of approximately twelve calendar days before the funds are made available. 

When I contacted Wells Fargo regarding the hold, I was advised that the deposit was considered " unusual. '' However, this explanation is inconsistent with my long-standing banking history. Over the years, I have deposited similar business checks in comparable amounts into this account without being subjected to an extended hold. The transaction was not materially different from prior deposits that Wells Fargo had routinely accepted and made available under its normal funds availability practices. 

I have also confirmed that the checks have cleared the issuing business account, meaning the funds have already been collected. Despite this, Wells Fargo continues to restrict my access to the deposited funds. 

The explanation provided by Wells Fargo appears unsupported by my account history and prior deposit activity. As a result, I am concerned that the stated reason for the hold does not accurately reflect the circumstances of the transaction. I am further concerned that Wells Fargo may be applying increasingly restrictive hold practices without conducting an individualized and reasonable assessment of the specific deposit involved. 

Based on my experience, this appears to represent a change in Wells Fargo 's treatment of deposited funds. The practical effect of these extended holds is that the bank retains use of customer funds for additional periods of time after collection has occurred, while customers are denied access to money that has already cleared. I believe this practice warrants regulatory review to determine whether it is consistent with applicable funds availability requirements and whether the reasons provided to customers for such holds are accurate, transparent, and supported by the facts. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate Wells Fargo 's handling of this deposit, review the basis for the extended hold, determine whether the bank 's actions comply with applicable regulations, and require Wells Fargo to provide a detailed explanation for why this deposit was classified as unusual despite a history of similar deposits being accepted without comparable restrictions.

complaint_what_happened:
I am submitting this complaint regarding TRUEACCORD because the company is reporting a collection account on my consumer credit reports that I do not recognize and do not believe belongs to me. I have never knowingly opened, authorized, applied for, or accepted responsibility for this alleged account. After discovering the account on my credit reports, I immediately reviewed my financial records and personal documentation in an effort to determine whether there was any legitimate connection between me and the debt being reported. Despite conducting a careful review of my records, I was unable to locate any contracts, agreements, account statements, billing records, payment histories, or other documentation demonstrating that I am responsible for this account. 

Because I do not recognize the account and have no knowledge of the debt being reported, I became concerned that my personal information may have been used without my authorization. As a result, I filed a report with the Federal Trade Commission and submitted an Identity Theft Report. I took these actions because I genuinely believe that this account may be the result of identity theft, unauthorized use of my personal information, inaccurate reporting, or a mixed-file error. I wanted to ensure that there was an official record documenting my claim that this debt is not mine and that I am disputing responsibility for the account. 

The TRUEACCORD account is currently being reported as a collection account with a derogatory status and an alleged balance of approximately {$450.00}. Although the amount may seem relatively small, the impact of a collection account on a consumer credit report is significant. Collection accounts are among the most damaging items that can appear on a credit report and can substantially reduce credit scores, increase borrowing costs, and negatively affect a consumer 's ability to obtain financing, housing, insurance, and employment opportunities. The continued reporting of an account that I do not own has caused unnecessary financial harm and has negatively affected my credit profile.

Upon discovering the account, I immediately disputed the information and requested a thorough investigation. I informed the appropriate parties that I did not recognize the account and that I had filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believed the debt may have resulted from identity theft. I requested documentation proving that I am legally responsible for the account, including any signed applications, contracts, agreements, billing statements, payment histories, account notes, records of communication, and any documents demonstrating that I knowingly entered into a financial relationship giving rise to the debt. 

Despite my dispute and identity theft claim, the account continues to be reported on my consumer credit reports. I have not been provided with sufficient documentation establishing that I am responsible for the debt. If TRUEACCORD believes that I owe this obligation, there should be clear evidence supporting that conclusion. Such evidence should include documentation identifying the original creditor, records showing when and how the account was opened, documentation establishing that I authorized the account, records demonstrating that I received goods, services, or funds associated with the debt, and documentation showing the legal basis for any collection activity. 

To date, I have not received information sufficient to establish that the account belongs to me. Instead, the account continues to appear on my credit reports despite my repeated efforts to dispute it and despite the existence of my FTC Identity Theft Report. I believe this is unfair and inconsistent with the requirement that information reported to consumer reporting agencies be accurate and verifiable. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires that furnishers and consumer reporting agencies maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of information reported about consumers. When a consumer disputes information and provides notice that the account may be the result of identity theft, a reasonable investigation must be conducted. Information that can not be verified should not continue to be reported. The continued reporting of a disputed collection account without adequate verification undermines the integrity of the consumer reporting system and causes unnecessary harm to consumers.

I am particularly concerned that my identity theft claim has not been given appropriate consideration. Identity theft is a serious problem that can affect consumers for years if fraudulent information remains on their credit reports. Federal law provides important protections for consumers who become victims of identity theft, and those protections exist to prevent consumers from being held responsible for debts they did not incur. When I filed my FTC Identity Theft Report, I expected that the account would receive heightened scrutiny and that meaningful efforts would be made to determine whether the debt actually belongs to me. 

Instead, the account continues to be reported, and I continue to experience the negative consequences associated with the derogatory information. Every day that this account remains on my credit reports, it has the potential to affect lending decisions, interest rates, housing opportunities, and other aspects of my financial life. Consumers should not be forced to suffer these consequences while inaccurate or fraudulent information remains unresolved.

I have acted responsibly throughout this process. Upon discovering the account, I reviewed my records, disputed the information, filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, and requested verification. I have fully cooperated and have made every reasonable effort to resolve the matter through the proper channels. Despite these efforts, the account remains on my credit reports and continues to damage my financial reputation.

I am requesting that TRUEACCORD conduct a comprehensive and independent investigation into this matter. I request that the company review all available records and determine whether there is competent evidence demonstrating that I knowingly opened, authorized, or benefited from the account. If the company can not establish through reliable documentation that I am legally responsible for the debt, the account should be immediately removed from all consumer reporting agencies.

I also request copies of all documents relied upon to verify the account. These documents should include the original account application, signed agreements, billing statements, payment histories, records identifying the original creditor, documentation showing assignment or transfer of the debt, and any other materials used to determine that I am responsible for the obligation. If such documents do not exist or can not be produced, the account should not continue to be reported.

In addition, I request that any derogatory information associated with this account be deleted. This includes collection status designations, derogatory remarks, adverse comments, delinquency indicators, and any other negative reporting connected to the account. Information that can not be verified should not remain on a consumer 's credit report.

I am also requesting transparency regarding the investigation process. If TRUEACCORD claims that the account has been verified, I would like a detailed explanation of the procedures used to reach that conclusion. I would like to know what records were reviewed, what evidence was relied upon, and how the company determined that the account belongs to me despite my FTC Identity Theft Report and formal dispute. Consumers deserve meaningful explanations when companies continue reporting disputed information.

The relief I am seeking is straightforward. I want TRUEACCORD to review my identity theft claim, conduct a thorough investigation, verify the account through competent evidence, and remove the account if it can not be substantiated. I also request that any corrections or deletions resulting from the investigation be communicated to all consumer reporting agencies so that my credit reports accurately reflect the outcome. 

I am not attempting to avoid responsibility for a legitimate debt. If documentation exists proving that I knowingly incurred the obligation, I am willing to review that information. However, I have not been provided with such documentation, and I continue to maintain that I do not own this account. Until competent evidence is produced, the account should not continue to be reported as a verified collection account.

In summary, I do not believe the TRUEACCORD collection account belongs to me. I discovered the account while reviewing my credit reports, disputed it immediately, and filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because I believe the account may be the result of identity theft or inaccurate reporting. Despite my efforts, the account continues to be reported and continues to negatively affect my credit profile. I respectfully request a full investigation, complete verification of the account through competent documentation, and permanent removal of the account and all associated derogatory information if TRUEACCORD can not establish that I am legally responsible for the debt. The issue is not whether XXXX XXXX  generated notices. 

The issue is whether XXXX XXXX  provided notice in a manner reasonably calculated to actually inform me of the cancellation of my homeowner 's insurance so that I could take action to protect my property before a catastrophic loss occurred. 

Federal law governing force-placed insurance, including RESPA and Regulation X ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.37 ), requires mortgage servicers to provide advance notice before obtaining force-placed insurance. The purpose of those notices is to provide borrowers a meaningful opportunity to obtain replacement coverage and avoid the very type of uninsured losses that occurred here.

I never received the notices upon which Rocket Mortgage now relies.

I anticipate Rocket Mortgage may argue that compliance was achieved because notices were generated and mailed. However, merely generating notices does not answer the critical question of whether those notices were directed in a manner reasonably calculated to provide actual notice under the circumstances known to the servicer.

The documents produced establish that : 1. A substitution of counsel had been filed with the court identifying new counsel and updated contact information.

2. XXXX XXXX  was actively involved in litigation concerning this loan through counsel representing the mortgage holder. 

3. XXXX XXXX  therefore had access to information reflecting the change in representation.

5. XXXX XXXX  subsequently mailed force-placed insurance correspondence directly to my residence on or about XX/XX/XXXX, demonstrating possession of my correct address. 

Accordingly, the issue is not whether XXXX XXXX  knew how to communicate with me. The issue is why the critical notices intended to prevent uninsured losses were not delivered in a manner reasonably calculated to reach me before XXXX XXXX. 

I further anticipate Rocket Mortgage may contend that I was independently responsible for maintaining insurance coverage.

I do not dispute my obligation to maintain insurance. However, that argument ignores the purpose of the federal notice requirements. The notice provisions exist specifically because Congress and regulators recognized that borrowers must be given an opportunity to correct a lapse before force-placed insurance is imposed and before significant harm occurs.

Had I received notice that my Florida XXXX policy had been cancelled, I would have immediately obtained replacement coverage. There was no reason for me to intentionally leave a residence of substantial value uninsured during hurricane season in Florida. 

Instead, I remained unaware of the cancellation until after XXXX XXXX caused catastrophic damage to my home and destroyed a substantial amount of personal property.

As a result, even if force-placed coverage technically existed, it did not place me in the same position that would have existed had I received notice and obtained replacement homeowner 's insurance.

The damages I sustained were foreseeable.

The purpose of the federal notice requirements is to prevent borrowers from unknowingly losing insurance protection and suffering uninsured losses.

In XX/XX/year>, U.S. Bank notified my husband and me that it had no record of insurance coverage for our property. 

We've had a US BANK HELOC on this property for over a decade, have never drawn on it to the best of my memory, and have insured the property continuously. 

We immediately submitted the requested insurance documentation through the bank 's designated portal, ihaveinsurance.com. 

After submitting the documents, U.S. Bank sent written confirmation via mail stating that it had received the information and that the insurance issue had been resolved. 

After receiving that written confirmation, we reasonably believed there were no remaining insurance deficiencies. 

In XX/XX/year>, U.S. Bank sent additional insurance-related letters. Because the bank had already informed us in writing that the insurance matter had been resolved, we were confused about why additional notices were being sent. 

Rather than ignore the letters, I immediately forwarded them to our XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and specifically sought guidance regarding whether any action was required. XXXX XXXX forwarded an inquiry to the insurance processing department and copied me. 

At that point, I believed I had done exactly what a customer should do : XXXX. Submitted the requested insurance documentation. 
XXXX. Received written confirmation from the bank that the issue was resolved. 
XXXX. Forwarded subsequent notices to the bank 's XXXX XXXX representative. 
XXXX. Requested guidance regarding any further action needed. 

Neither XXXX XXXX nor anyone else from U.S. Bank informed me that : The new notices allegedly concerned a separate wind insurance requirement ( which to our knowledge, had never been required in the past ) The bank considered us non-compliant ; Force-placed insurance was being contemplated ; Failure to take additional action could result in over {$5000.00} dollars in charges being added to the HELOC ; or Immediate action was required to avoid force-placement. 

Because I had already received written confirmation that the insurance issue was resolved and because I had escalated the subsequent notices to the bank 's XXXX XXXX representative and heard nothing back, I reasonably believed the matter had been addressed. 

Importantly, I did not ignore the notices. I forwarded them to the bank and asked for assistance. No one including XXXX XXXX called me or emailed me to explain there was still a problem. 

Force-Placed Insurance On XX/XX/year>, we received a letter dated XX/XX/year>, informing us that U.S. Bank XXXX XXXX wind insurance on the property retroactive to XX/XX/year>, at a cost of {$5400.00}. 

This was the first time we understood that U.S. Bank believed any insurance issue remained unresolved. 

I immediately contacted XXXX XXXX and sought assistance and although he had been my primary contact at the bank for about a decade he referred me to the loan department and was unwilling to help me. 

A U.S. Bank loan representative in the loan department then informed me that the bank had repeatedly communicated by phone with our insurance carrier regarding the alleged deficiency. However, neither my husband nor I received a direct phone call or email, from U.S. Bank explaining that force-placed insurance was imminent or that a {$5400.00} charge would be imposed. Again, no one in XXXX XXXX, who had handled everything for us for over a decade, communicated a word to us despite repeated inquiries! 

Had anyone just explained that wind coverage was allegedly missing and that force-placed insurance would otherwise be purchased, we would have immediately resolved the issue or simply closed the unused HELOC. 

Excessive Insurance Cost After learning of the force-placed coverage, our insurance agent quoted us {$1700.00} for comparable wind, hurricane, etc. coverage. 

U.S. Bank charged {$5400.00} for force-placed coveragemore than XXXX times the quoted market cost. 

Contradictory Information Regarding HELOC Closure Once I became aware of the issue, I immediately and repeatedly requested closure of the unused HELOC. 

I was pleased that in XX/XX/year>, U.S. Bank sent me a written letter stating that nothing was due on the HELOC and that I simply needed to sign and return a document if I wished to close the account. Seemed clear that they waived the forced placed insurance fee. 

However, when I subsequently contacted the bank to complete the closure process, I was told that the {$5400.00} force-placed insurance charge had to be paid before the HELOC could be closed. 

These contradictory statements created further confusion. On XXXX hand, the bank 's written communication stated that nothing was due and only a closure form was required. On the other hand, bank representatives informed me that a substantial balance had to be paid before closure would be allowed. 

Unauthorized Duplicate Withdrawal On XX/XX/year>, a U.S. Bank loan servicing representative, XXXX ( Badge # ZVQ ), advised me that paying the {$5400.00} charge would stop additional insurance-related charges from accruing while my request for review, refund, and closure remained pending. 

Based on that representation, I authorized a single payment of {$5400.00} and again requested closure of the HELOC. 

The following day, U.S. Bank generated notices showing that XXXX separate withdrawals of {$5400.00} had been initiated from my linked XXXX XXXX Bank account. 

I authorized only XXXX payment. 

The second withdrawal was unauthorized. 

When I contacted U.S. Bank, I was informed that the bank would not immediately return the improperly withdrawn funds and that I would instead have to wait approximately XXXX weeks for reimbursement by paper check. 

As a result, U.S. Bank removed an additional {$5400.00} from my account without authorization and retained possession of those funds while requiring me to wait for the bank 's internal correction process. 

Why I Believe U.S. Bank Acted Improperly This situation appears to involve potential violations of federal mortgage-servicing and consumer-protection requirements, including : Failure to provide clear and effective notice before charging force-placed insurance as required under Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.37 ; Failure to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining insurance information already provided by the borrower ; Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, including sending written confirmation that an insurance issue was resolved while later imposing force-placed insurance based on allegedly unresolved coverage concerns ; Providing contradictory information regarding whether any balance was due before HELOC closure ; Unauthorized electronic fund withdrawal and failure to promptly correct the error after removing funds that were not authorized by the account holder.
